title: Prince of the Creeks
teaser: Mangroves, mist and a midnight ambush. Someone doesn't want Tari to reach Port Harcourt alive.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bayelsa. Mist on the creeks, and mangrove roots reaching into the water like old men's fingers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tari Ebiowei had been on the water since four. The fishermen had already told him. The Chief was dead.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: He pulled me out of this river when I was six. Raised me like his own. And I wasn't there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fishermen tell it differently. They say a woman in white pulled the boy out of the creek, and the Chief only found him on the bank. Some nights, Tari isn't sure they are wrong.

lines.speaker: letter
lines.text: Tari. You were the son I chose. Protect the girl from the Rock. Nabyen. Do not let them near her. — G.O.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: Nabyen? Little Nabyen from Jos? She used to scream at every fish.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In his jacket, folded small, is a note he has written a hundred times and never signed with his own name. A red hibiscus is pressed inside. At the bottom, one letter: W.

choices.text: "Gather the crew. We sail for Port Harcourt tonight."

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Twelve boats. Twelve men. Every one of them owes the Chief their life.

choices.text: Go alone. Fewer eyes, fewer mouths.

response.speaker: tari
response.text: If someone poisoned an old lion in his own house, they'll be watching the river.

choices.text: "First, I find out who killed him."

response.speaker: tari
response.text: Old men don't die of 'tiredness' the same week they rewrite their will. Somebody did this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His phone rings. Port Harcourt. The widow.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: Tari. You will stay away from the funeral. My husband's charity ended when his heart stopped.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: This is family business, and you are not family.

scenes.prompt: Ibiere Okoro, the Chief's widow, wants him gone.

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Then come. And see how quickly respect runs out.

choices.text: "Of course, Madam. I'll stay in the creeks."
"Madam, who was with him the night he died?"

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She hangs up, but not before he hears another woman's voice in the room. An accent. French, or Swiss.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Midnight on the creeks. No moon cover, no engines but his own.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then another engine. Fast. Lights off.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: DOWN!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bullets chew the mangroves. A speedboat swings past, and something heavy splashes into the water beside him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One of the attackers has gone overboard. He can't swim.

scenes.prompt: The speedboat is getting away. The man in the water is going under.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: He loses them in the mangroves, but they drop something in the chase: a bank card. First Lagoon Bank, Lagos.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Tari hauls him into the boat, coughing up river.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: For a moment, under the black water, Tari sees a pale hand pushing the man up towards him. Then it is gone.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: 'The white woman pays in francs,' the man gasps. 'She said nobody from the creeks reaches Port Harcourt.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dawn. The Port Harcourt jetty. Tari ties up the boat with hands that won't stop shaking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And there at the end of the jetty, in an orange ankara dress, is a woman he hasn't seen since she was twelve.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Tari? Tari Ebiowei? Since when are you so tall?

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: You still owe me a fish, you know. A big one. You promised.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She has a red rose petal pinned inside her collar. Tari recognises it. He should. He sent it.

choices.text: Pull her into a hug. Fish later.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: Okay. Okay! You smell like the river.

choices.text: "Someone tried to kill me last night. Stay close."
"Miss Dalyop. The Chief asked me to look after you."

outcomes.title: Blood in the Water
outcomes.text: A Lagos bank card, dropped by men who tried to kill him. Tari now has a name to hate. It might even be the right one.

outcomes.title: The Woman Who Pays in Francs
outcomes.text: Someone far from the creeks is paying in Swiss money for Nigerian blood.

outcomes.title: Turning Tide
outcomes.text: Tari reached Port Harcourt alive. On the creeks, that's a kind of victory.

reflections.text: Something old and warm is waking up between the captain and the girl from the rocks.
Twelve boats answer to Tari now.
Ibiere thinks Tari is in the creeks. She'll find out soon.

s_swear.title: An oath on the water
s_swear.text: SWEAR, from the waters. Tari's father swore on the Nun River to protect the Chief, and died keeping that oath. The Chief never forgave himself.

m_creeks.title: Mist on the Creeks
m_creeks.text: Mangroves, a canoe, and news nobody wanted to deliver.

m_night_creek.title: Ambush at Midnight
m_night_creek.text: Fireflies, bullets, and a man who couldn't swim.

k_francs.title: A wet ten-franc note
k_francs.text: What a life costs on the creeks, apparently. Paid in Swiss money.

epigraph.text: What the creek takes, the creek keeps.
